title: No instinct exists for the exclusive good of another species

fields.label: Label
fields.value: No instinct exists for the exclusive good of another species

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: No animal performs an instinctive action solely for the benefit of another species, although each species takes advantage of the instincts of others.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Although I do not believe that any animal in the world performs an action for the exclusive good of another of a distinct species, yet each species tries to take advantage of the instincts of others

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VII, “Instinct”; section “Aphides and ants”. Scope: interspecific behavioural interactions among all animals, including mutualisms such as aphid–ant associations

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch07-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.39

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing records can screen for candidate behaviours but cannot settle exclusivity for all animals. Focused systems are testable only partially.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Identify interspecific helping behaviours and estimate lifetime direct and inclusive-fitness effects for actor and recipient. A heritable instinct with benefit exclusively to the other species and no compensating actor benefit would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Proving zero actor benefit is exceptionally difficult.

Databases record interactions, not complete fitness accounting.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.34
discriminating power: 0.36
data adequacy: 0.22
data existence: 0.57
operationalizability: 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Interaction data can flag mutualisms and manipulations for follow-up, which is a restricted proxy for the universal negative. The decisive measurement, fitness to the actor versus fitness only to another species, is scattered through experiments and missing for nearly all interactions. Analysis at the stated scope is not a weeks-scale job on existing tables.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Among recorded interspecific behaviors, test whether any instinct increases another species' fitness while leaving the actor and its kin with no fitness gain. One such instinct would refute the claim; finding that apparent gifts, such as aphid honeydew or cleaner-fish service, return a benefit to the actor supports it only as a partial screen.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Exploitation of another species' instinct is easily confused with an instinct performed for that species.

The universal wording cannot be confirmed by absence of a known case.

GloBI does not encode instinct, exclusive benefit, or fitness.
